text: Gestation — from conception to calving — lasts an average of 285 days, during which the cow shows no oestrus signs. Because of this, checking carefully for a return to heat about 3 weeks after mating is important to confirm pregnancy. After 7 months of pregnancy, physical evidence of gestation can be seen on the cow's right side. The placenta connects the fetus to the uterine wall, delivering nutrients and removing waste and exchanging oxygen/carbon dioxide via the cow's blood; cattle have a cotyledonary placenta with about 75–125 oval caruncles acting like many small individual placentas. The placenta is normally delivered within 6 to 12 hours of birth.
